prompt:
Edit the supplied C dashboard mockup into the FINAL PROPOSED COMPOSITION with integrated expandable technical drawer. High-fidelity implementable desktop web UI, 1536x1024 landscape, English copy. Keep its left scenario rail, navy/cobalt/white palette, readable sans typography, flat restrained dividers and the clear request/reply diagram. This is a static design mockup with illustrative data.

CRITICAL CHANGE: REMOVE BOTH "Guided demo" AND "Technical controls" TOP TABS ENTIRELY. No main-view tabs and no replacement tab strip. Each sidebar scenario is one unified page. The main page contains the guided demonstration plus a bottom expandable technical panel, OPEN in this mockup. The panel is part of the same page, not a modal, overlay, terminal window or second route.

LAYOUT:
- Left rail remains about 220px wide, full height. Logo/title "Idempotent requests lab". SCENARIOS with exactly the existing six items, Lost reply selected: Send twice; Lost reply; Send together; Fail before saving; Change content; Create another. "2 of 6" at bottom.
- Main workspace width fills the remaining viewport. Very compact top bar with "Scenario 02 / 06" left and small "Local demo" status right. No tabs.
- Compact heading "Lost reply" and one line "The request is saved. The reply never arrives."
- A simplified, shorter version of the supplied diagram in the upper middle. Monitor left titled "Your screen", purple badge "Unconfirmed". Server right titled "Server", green badge "Saved", small "Pump inspection". Upper solid outgoing arrow labelled "Request sent" goes fully left-to-right to server. Lower return arrow points toward monitor but is broken in the center at an X labelled "Reply lost". Do not let the outgoing request stop at the X; only the return reply is lost. Exactly one saved request.
- Compact counter row "1 send" and "1 saved request" under diagram.
- An action row stays ABOVE the technical drawer: small "Show explanation" disclosure on left and the only cobalt primary button "Retry same request" on right. The primary action stays visible while the drawer is open.
- Bottom docked EXPANDABLE TECHNICAL DRAWER spans ONLY the main workspace, leaving the sidebar fully visible. About bottom 32% of viewport. It reflows/compresses the content above instead of covering anything. Distinct pale cool-gray surface, thin top border, small centered resize grip. Header row has a code icon, "Technical details", compact "1 attempt" badge, and "Collapse" plus downward chevron at far right. This entire header is the collapse/expand affordance.
- Drawer body TWO COLUMNS separated by a quiet vertical rule, no tabs inside. Left wider column title "HTTP activity". One compact timeline/table entry with tiny time "14:32:01", verb "POST", path "/interventions", and violet outlined badge "No response". A short monospace line beneath says "Response body unavailable". Beneath that, a second concise evidence row labelled "Saved record" with green check and "1 request found". Clearly distinguish missing client response from saved server record; never show HTTP 201 as received.
- Right narrower drawer column title "Request & tools". Two compact label/value rows "Idempotency key" with abbreviated "3f93…2a71" and copy icon; "Saved request" with abbreviated "9b31…e62c" and copy icon. Then label "Next attempt" with a compact native-looking select displaying "Normal delivery". Under it a quiet outlined button "Refresh records" and a collapsed disclosure "Advanced tools". Advanced tools will contain manual payload editing, clock, purge and reset; do NOT expand them or show destructive red controls by default.
- Everything fits the viewport, with clear boundaries, no overlaps, no giant blank areas, no paragraphs. Stronger visual emphasis remains on the guided result and main retry button, not the technical drawer. Drawer text is readable, compact and has monospace only for technical values. No decorative charts, generated claims, chat bubbles or analytics tiles. Do not add any text explaining the design, any mockup annotation, or the words Guided demo / Technical controls anywhere. Preserve the exact scenario and its truth: one sent request, one saved record, uncertain client until the next retry.
status: Final proposed C composition with technical drawer expanded; illustrative data, not runtime evidence
userDirection: C selected as the base; remove both top tabs and integrate scenario-specific technical controls in an expandable bottom panel
approval: User approved implementation on 2026-10-15; one page per scenario, technical panel collapsed by default.
